# #009. Shadow Prices & Bottleneck Analysis

<!-- section:scenario -->
Beyond computing the optimal continuous production vector `quantities[j]` for resource limits `capacities[k]` and margins `margins[j]`, operations leaders need to know **which capacity bottlenecks limit profit** and **how much 1 additional unit of resource $k$ is worth at the margin**.

Solve the production maximization LP and return the optimal quantities, profit, **shadow prices (`c.dual` / `row_dual`)**, **unused slack (`c.slack` / `cap - row_value`)**, and a boolean flag `isBottleneck[k]` indicating whether expanding resource $k$ directly improves maximum profit (`shadowPrices[k] > 1e-5` / tight constraint).

<!-- section:io -->
- **Input (`P009Input`)**:
  - `margins: number[]` — profit per unit of product $j$
  - `usages: number[][]` — `usages[k][j]` consumption of resource $k$ per unit of product $j$
  - `capacities: number[]` — available capacity of each resource $k$
- **Output (`P009Output`)**:
  - `quantities: number[]` — optimal production levels
  - `optimalProfit: number` — maximum profit
  - `shadowPrices: number[]` — LP dual values $y_k \ge 0$ (marginal profit per unit increase of `capacities[k]`)
  - `slacks: number[]` — unused capacity `capacities[k] - sum_j usages[k][j] * quantities[j]`
  - `isBottleneck: boolean[]` — `true` iff resource $k$ is an active bottleneck (`shadowPrices[k] > 1e-5`)

<!-- section:example -->
In Case 1 (`margins = [50, 40]`, `usages = [[2, 1], [1, 2], [1, 1]]`, `capacities = [100, 80, 70]`):

- Optimal production is `quantities = [40, 20]`, yielding profit **`2,800`**.
- Resources 0 and 1 are fully consumed (`slack = 0`) with shadow prices **`20`** and **`10`**: buying 1 extra unit of resource 0 raises max profit from `2,800` to `2,820`!
- Resource 2 only uses `40 + 20 = 60 <= 70`, leaving `slack = 10`, so its marginal value **`shadowPrices[2] = 0`** (complementary slackness!). Notice strong duality holds: `100*20 + 80*10 + 70*0 = 2,800`.

<!-- section:hint1 -->
Keep references to the constraint objects you create when building the model!
- **WaSHI (`TypeScript`)**: `const c = m.constraint(...)`, then after `await m.solve()` read **`c.dual`** and **`c.slack`**!
- **Python (`highspy`)**: `c = h.addConstr(...)`, solve, then call `sol = h.getSolution()` and read **`sol.row_dual[c.index]`** and **`cap - sol.row_value[c.index]`**.

<!-- section:hint2 -->
Remember the three pillars of LP duality that our automated judge checks independently:
1. **Dual Feasibility**: `shadowPrices[k] >= 0` and $\sum_k \text{usages}[k][j] \, y_k \ge \text{margins}[j]$ for all $j$.
2. **Complementary Slackness**: `slacks[k] * shadowPrices[k] == 0` (unused capacity cannot have positive shadow price).
3. **Strong Duality**: $\sum_k \text{capacities}[k] \, y_k = \text{optimalProfit}$.

<!-- section:formulation -->
$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{(Primal)} \quad \max_{x \ge 0} \; c^\top x \quad \text{s.t.} \; Ax \le b
\qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad
\text{(Dual)} \quad \min_{y \ge 0} \; b^\top y \quad \text{s.t.} \; A^\top y \ge c
\end{aligned}
$$

By strong duality, $c^\top x^* = b^\top y^*$ and $y_k^* = \frac{\partial V^*(b)}{\partial b_k}$ (non-degenerate marginal value of capacity $k$).

judge.m0: Output must be an object { quantities, optimalProfit, shadowPrices, slacks, isBottleneck }.
judge.m1: isBottleneck must be a boolean array of length {p0}.
judge.m4: slacks[{p0}] ({p1}) does not match unused capacity ({p2}).
judge.m5: Reported optimalProfit ({p0}) does not match profit from quantities ({p1}).
judge.m6: Feasible plan, but profit ({p0}) is below LP optimum ({p1}).
judge.m7: shadowPrices[{p0}] must be >= 0 for <= capacity constraints in maximization (got {p1}).
judge.m8: Complementary slackness violated: resource {p0} has positive slack ({p1}), so its shadowPrice must be 0 (got {p2}).
judge.m10: Dual feasibility failed for product {p0}: imputed resource value ({p1}) < margin ({p2}).
judge.m11: Strong duality failed: sum(capacities * shadowPrices) = {p0} != optimalProfit ({p1}).
judge.m12: Optimal plan + verified shadow prices (profit = {p0}, duals = [{p1}])!
